scope: M101 B01 U01 L03; seven sections, seven worked examples, seven in-text activities, eight figures (six original diagrams and two sourced photographs). No new interactive or video: static constructions serve this lesson; scalar exploration already exists in L02. Unit-end mixed exercises and PDF remain due at unit completion.

calibration.source: OU MST124 Unit 5 pp138–139, 171–172; Activity43 and its solution
calibration.comparison: Distinguish vector from scalar magnitude; derive with right triangle; exact square roots before decimals. Practice includes signed components, displacement from endpoints, and route versus separation; original prompts and numbers.

calibration.source: OU MST124 Unit5 pp171–172, Activity43; OpenStax Calculus3 §2.2 Example2.19
calibration.comparison: Two right triangles precede 3D formula; include missing component with two signs, endpoint subtraction and a component lower-bound check. Source practice informs level, not wording.

calibration.source: OU MST124 Unit5 scalar-multiplication discussion pp144–148; OpenStax Calculus3 §2.1 vector operations
calibration.comparison: Retrieve scaling, derive absolute-value magnitude rule, contrast sum of magnitudes with magnitude of sum. Original sign, zero and equal-length counterexamples.

calibration.source: OU MST124 Unit5 pp156–157 (coordinate unit vectors); OpenStax Calculus3 §2.1 Unit Vectors, Example2.7, Checkpoint2.8 and Example2.8; §2.2 Example2.19
calibration.comparison: OU excerpt supplies coordinate-basis presentation but is insufficient for arbitrary normalisation. OpenStax supplements same-direction unit vector and prescribed-length construction. Separate normalising, basis notation and reconstruction; explicitly treat zero, units, opposite direction and vectors shorter than one. Original examples/practice, including diagnostic incorrect answers.
Original cumulative endpoint/step problem combines component subtraction, length, unit direction and reconstruction. Does not introduce angle prerequisites or substitute for full-unit exercise set.

arithmetic.scope: Independent arithmetic checks; geometric reasoning and derivations reviewed separately.

revisions: Added an explicit short-vector example: normalising can lengthen, not just shrink.

Clarified numerical model is invented, not a measurement inferred from the Astrobee photograph.
